# Qatar TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT

## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS

Obtain local mobile connectivity with ease. Two main providers offer extensive coverage and competitive plans.

#### Key Information to Research

| **Aspect**            | **Details to Find**                                                                                                      |
| :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Providers**         | Ooredoo, Vodafone                                                                                                        |
| **Price Options**     | Tourist SIM packages from QAR 35 (approx. $10) for 7-day to QAR 100+ for 30-day options with varying data/calls.         |
| **Data Allocation**   | Plans range from 1GB to unlimited data, with high-speed limits before throttling.                                        |
| **Validity Period**   | 7-day, 14-day, 30-day plans are common for tourists.                                                                     |
| **Hotspot/Tethering** | Generally allowed on most plans.                                                                                         |
| **Coverage**          | Excellent 4G/5G coverage across Qatar, including major cities and desert areas.                                          |
| **Where to Buy**      | Hamad International Airport (HIA) arrivals hall, Ooredoo/Vodafone official stores in malls, electronics shops.           |
| **Alternative: eSIM** | Options like Airalo, Holafly, Nomad offer Qatar-specific or regional eSIMs starting from $5-10 for small data packages. |

#### Recommendations Framework

*   **Short trips (3-7 days):** A 7-day tourist SIM from the airport is convenient, offering enough data for navigation and communication.
*   **Staying 1-4 weeks:** Opt for a 30-day plan with higher data allocation from Ooredoo or Vodafone.
*   **Digital nomad preferences:** eSIM offers flexibility to switch plans and avoid physical SIM hassle, though activation can be slightly more complex.
*   **Budget-conscious:** Compare entry-level tourist packages directly at the airport kiosks for the best value per data GB.

## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS

Navigate efficiently from Hamad International Airport (HIA) to Doha city center.

**Route**: From Hamad International Airport (HIA) to Doha Corniche/West Bay area

| **Mode**                     | **Duration**       | **Cost**                       | **Booking**                    | **Convenience** | **Best For**                                |
| :--------------------------- | :----------------- | :----------------------------- | :----------------------------- | :-------------- | :------------------------------------------ |
| **Doha Metro**               | ~20-30 mins        | QAR 2 (Standard) / QAR 10 (Gold) | HIA Metro Station              | Excellent       | Speed, budget, no traffic, single travelers |
| **Karwa Taxi (Metered)**     | 20-40 mins         | QAR 30-50                      | Airport taxi stand, Karwa app  | Very Good       | Door-to-door, groups, luggage, reliable     |
| **Ride-hailing (Uber/Careem)** | 20-40 mins         | QAR 30-60                      | App-based                      | Very Good       | Door-to-door, pre-booked, late night        |
| **Airport Bus (Karwa)**      | 45-60 mins         | QAR 2.5-10                     | HIA Bus Pavilion               | Good            | Budget travelers, scenic route              |
| **Hotel Shuttle**            | Depends            | Varies                         | Contact hotel prior            | Good            | Convenience, pre-arranged                   |
| **Car Rental**               | Flexible           | Moderate-High                  | Online agencies, HIA counters  | Excellent       | Exploration, independence                   |

#### Detail Each Option With

*   **Doha Metro**: The Red Line connects HIA to key city areas. Board at HIA Metro Station (Gate A on arrival). Frequency is every 5-10 minutes. Final drop-off at stations like National Museum, Souq Waqif, or West Bay. Purchase travel cards from vending machines or ticket counters. Operates roughly 06:00-23:00 Sat-Wed, 06:00-23:59 Thu, 14:00-23:59 Fri.
*   **Karwa Taxi (Metered)**: Found immediately outside the arrivals hall. Look for the distinctive turquoise taxis. No pre-booking needed for airport queue. Drop-off at any desired city location. Purchase via meter. Operates 24/7.
*   **Ride-hailing (Uber/Careem)**: Book via app after connecting to airport Wi-Fi. Pick-up points are clearly marked outside arrivals. Upfront pricing shown in app. Operates 24/7.
*   **Airport Bus (Karwa)**: Located at the Bus Pavilion outside the terminal. Route 747 serves key city stops. Purchase a Karwa Smartcard from airport vending machines. Frequencies vary (every 20-30 mins). Operates roughly 04:40-23:00.

## 3. CURRENCY EXCHANGE

Convert home currency to Qatari Riyal (QAR) at competitive rates.

**Current Exchange Rate**: 1 USD = ~3.64 QAR (fixed rate)

#### Best Exchange Locations

| **Location**         | **Why It's Best**          | **Address**                               | **Hours**                 | **Rates**           | **Tips**                                        |
| :------------------- | :------------------------- | :---------------------------------------- | :------------------------ | :------------------ | :---------------------------------------------- |
| **Qatar National Bank** | Reliable, official rates   | Numerous branches across Doha             | Standard banking hours    | Official              | Good for larger amounts, secure                 |
| **Al Fardan Exchange** | Competitive rates, many branches | City Center Mall, Villaggio Mall, etc.    | Mall opening hours        | Very competitive    | Check multiple branches for slight variations   |
| **Souq Waqif Money Changers** | Convenient, good rates     | Within Souq Waqif, near main entrances    | Approx. 09:00-13:00, 16:00-22:00 | Good                | Compare rates of 2-3 shops before committing    |

#### Alternative Methods

| **Method**           | **Pros**                         | **Cons**                                    | **Best For**            |
| :------------------- | :------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------ | :---------------------- |
| **ATM Withdrawal**   | Widely available, mid-market rates | Bank fees (local and home bank), limits     | Convenient, accessible  |
| **Airport Exchange** | Immediate access upon arrival      | Slightly less favorable rates               | Emergency small amounts |
| **Credit Card**      | Secure, widely accepted            | Foreign transaction fees (check with bank)  | Large purchases         |
| **Bank Transfer**    | Best rates if pre-arranged         | Time-consuming, specific purpose            | Planned payments        |

#### Universal Tips

*   The Qatari Riyal (QAR) is pegged to the US Dollar (USD) at a fixed rate of 1 USD = 3.64 QAR, so rates are consistent.
*   Avoid exchanging at small hotel desks, which typically offer worse rates.
*   Have small QAR denominations for taxis or small purchases.
*   ATMs are plentiful throughout the city and at the airport.

## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS

Experience authentic Qatari and Middle Eastern cuisine.

🍽️ **Machboos (مجبوس)** – Main Course
→ What: Qatar's national dish; spiced rice (often basmati) with tender meat (lamb, chicken, or camel) or fish, slow-cooked to perfection.
→ Where: Al Jasra Traditional Arabic Food (Souq Waqif), Damasca One.
→ Price: QAR 40-80
→ Try with: Daqoos (tomato sauce), fresh salad, and yogurt.

🍽️ **Thareed (ثريد)** – Main Course/Stew
→ What: A hearty stew of vegetables (potatoes, carrots, beans) and meat, served over thin pieces of bread (regag), which absorb the rich broth.
→ Where: Shay Al Shamoos, local Qatari restaurants.
→ Price: QAR 35-65
→ Try with: Lemon wedges for a tangy finish.

🍽️ **Harees (هريس)** – Main Course
→ What: A thick porridge-like dish made from boiled, cracked wheat mixed with meat (usually chicken or lamb) and seasoned with spices.
→ Where: Popular during Ramadan, but found in traditional restaurants year-round.
→ Price: QAR 30-50
→ Try with: Melted ghee (clarified butter) and a sprinkle of cinnamon.

🍽️ **Luqaimat (لقيمات)** – Dessert
→ What: Sweet, crispy fried dough balls, similar to doughnuts, drenched in honey or date syrup.
→ Where: Various dessert shops, Souq Waqif food stalls, traditional cafes.
→ Price: QAR 15-25 (per plate)
→ Try with: Karak Tea for a perfect sweet and savory combo.

☕ **Karak Tea (شاي كرك)** – Beverage
→ What: A strong, milky, sweet tea brewed with black tea, sugar, and cardamom, and often other spices like ginger.
→ Where: Widely available at cafeterias, roadside stalls, and cafes across Qatar.
→ Price: QAR 2-5 (per cup)
→ Try with: Any local snack or simply as a daily ritual.

## 7. SUPERMARKETS & CONVENIENCE STORES

Access everyday items, snacks, and groceries conveniently.

**Major Supermarket Chains**

*   **Carrefour**: Best for wide selection of international and local goods, electronics, and household items. Several large hypermarkets (Villaggio Mall, City Center Mall) and smaller Carrefour Market stores. Hours typically 08:00-23:00.
*   **Lulu Hypermarket**: Known for competitive prices, especially on groceries, fresh produce, and Indian/Asian products. Very popular with residents. Located throughout Doha. Hours typically 08:00-23:00.
*   **Monoprix**: Upscale French supermarket offering premium imported goods, organic produce, and a good deli selection. Found in high-end malls like Place Vendôme, Doha Festival City. Hours typically 08:00-23:00.
*   **Al Meera**: Qatar's national supermarket chain, widely distributed in residential areas, offering essential groceries and local products. Known for reasonable prices. Hours typically 07:00-23:00.

**Convenience Stores**

*   **Panda**: Small convenience stores offering snacks, drinks, and basic necessities. Many locations, often 24/7.
*   **Woqod (Sidra)**: Found at petrol stations, offering a quick stop for snacks, drinks, and basic travel essentials. Often 24/7.

**Pharmacy Chains**

*   **Boots Pharmacy**: International chain with a wide range of health, beauty, and wellness products. Found in most major malls.
*   **Kulud Pharmacy**: Local chain, widely available, offering prescription and over-the-counter medications.

## 8. DAY & NIGHT MARKETS

Experience local culture, find unique goods, and enjoy street food.

#### Night Markets
Most of Doha's traditional markets (souqs) come alive in the evenings.

| **Market Name** | **Location**       | **Open Hours**             | **Best For**              | **What to Expect**                                | **Pro Tips**                                    |
| :-------------- | :----------------- | :------------------------- | :------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------- |
| **Souq Waqif**  | Al Souq Street, Doha | 09:00-12:30, 16:00-22:00 (daily) | Souvenirs, spices, local food, art | Traditional Qatari architecture, bustling atmosphere, falcon shops | Go after sunset for the best ambiance; try street food and karak tea. |

#### Day Markets
Souq Waqif also operates during the day, offering a quieter experience.

| **Market Name** | **Location**       | **Open Hours**             | **Best For**              | **What to Expect**                               | **Pro Tips**                                 |
| :-------------- | :----------------- | :------------------------- | :------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------- |
| **Souq Waqif**  | Al Souq Street, Doha | 09:00-12:30, 16:00-22:00 (daily) | Spices, textiles, crafts, gold | Less crowded than evening, good for relaxed browsing | Visit in the morning to avoid heat and crowds. |

#### Specialty Markets

*   **Gold Souq**: Located adjacent to Souq Waqif, specializing in intricate gold jewelry (22K and 24K). Bargaining is expected.
*   **Falcon Souq**: Also within Souq Waqif, a unique market dedicated to falcons and falconry accessories, a key part of Qatari heritage.
*   **Fish Market (Al Wakra Souq)**: Modern, clean market for fresh seafood. Located south of Doha in Al Wakra.

#### Universal Night/Day Market Tips

*   Carry Qatari Riyal in smaller denominations as many smaller vendors do not accept cards.
*   Bargaining is expected in Souq Waqif, especially for non-food items. Start by offering about 50-70% of the asking price.
*   Dress modestly out of respect for local culture.
*   Stay hydrated, especially during the day.

## 9. BEST ALCOHOLIC DRINKS

Understand Qatar's regulations and limited options for alcoholic beverages.

Qatar has strict laws regarding alcohol. It is illegal to drink alcohol in public places. Alcohol is only available to visitors in licensed hotel restaurants and bars. Residents can purchase alcohol from a single designated distributor with a permit.

#### Local Beers
There is no local beer production in Qatar. Imported international brands are available in licensed venues.

| **Brand** | **Type**    | **Flavor Profile** | **Where to Buy**                 | **Price**      | **Try At**            |
| :-------- | :---------- | :----------------- | :------------------------------- | :------------- | :-------------------- |
| **Heineken** | Lager       | Crisp, light       | Licensed hotel bars/restaurants  | QAR 40-60 ($11-16) | West Bay hotels, Pearl-Qatar |
| **Budweiser** | Lager       | Mild, refreshing   | Licensed hotel bars/restaurants  | QAR 40-60 ($11-16) | Sports bars in hotels |
| **Stella Artois** | Pilsner     | Clean, hoppy       | Licensed hotel bars/restaurants  | QAR 45-65 ($12-18) | Upscale hotel lounges |

#### Spirits & Liqueurs
Only international brands are available.

| **Drink**   | **Type**   | **Origin**      | **Taste**             | **Where to Buy**                | **Price**              |
| :---------- | :--------- | :-------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------------ | :--------------------- |
| **Gin & Tonic** | Cocktail   | International   | Refreshing, botanical | Licensed hotel bars/restaurants | QAR 50-80 ($14-22)     |
| **Whisky**  | Spirit     | International   | Varies by type        | Licensed hotel bars/restaurants | QAR 60-120 ($16-33) per glass |

#### Wine & Rice Wine
No local wine or rice wine production. International wines are available in licensed venues.

#### Where to Buy

| **Outlet Type**           | **Best For**                       | **Price Level** | **Selection**      |
| :------------------------ | :--------------------------------- | :-------------- | :----------------- |
| **Licensed Hotel Bars**   | Immediate consumption, wide variety | High            | Good, international |
| **Duty-free (HIA Arrivals)** | Personal consumption for residents with permits | Discount        | Large              |

#### Drinking Culture Tips

*   Legal drinking age is 21.
*   Alcohol is only sold and consumed in licensed hotel restaurants, bars, and clubs. It is illegal to purchase or consume alcohol outside these venues.
*   Public intoxication is strictly prohibited and can lead to severe penalties.
*   Tipping customs in bars: 10-15% is common if service charge not included.
*   Peak drinking hours are typically Thursday and Friday evenings.

## BONUS SECTIONS

### 11. LOCAL CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE

Respecting local customs in Qatar is crucial for a pleasant visit. This section outlines key cultural guidelines.

#### 11a. Mosque & Sacred Site Dress Code

Dress codes at mosques and other religious sites in Qatar are strictly enforced.

| **Rule**                | **What to Check**                                | **Enforcement Level**         |
| :---------------------- | :----------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------- |
| **Shoulders covered**   | Sleeveless tops / tank tops prohibited for both men and women | Strictly enforced             |
| **Knees covered**       | Shorts / mini-skirts prohibited for both men and women | Strictly enforced             |
| **Footwear**            | Shoes removed before entry into prayer halls     | Mandatory                     |
| **Head covering**       | Required for women entering mosques              | Mandatory for women           |
| **Colour restrictions** | None                                             | Not applicable                |
| **Sarong/Wrap rental**  | Sometimes available at major tourist mosques for women | Common at State Grand Mosque  |

> T-shirts and lightweight long pants are the perfect outfit for visiting religious sites – simple, cool, and always accepted.

> **Qatar-specific rules:** Both men and women must dress modestly in public, covering shoulders and knees. This is particularly important when visiting mosques and government buildings. Women should carry a scarf to cover their heads if planning to enter a mosque.

#### 11b. The Head, Feet & Body — Cultural Hierarchy

Qatari and Islamic cultures consider the left hand as unclean, and showing the soles of your feet as disrespectful.

> Never touch another person’s head. When passing objects or eating, always use your right hand. Avoid pointing the soles of your feet towards people or any revered object.

> **Qatar-specific:** Use your right hand for greetings, eating, and handling objects. The left hand is traditionally associated with personal hygiene.

#### 11c. Religious Etiquette

Religious figures and places of worship hold deep respect.

| **Rule**                         | **Detail**                                                             | **Who It Applies To**     |
| :------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------ |
| **Physical contact with opposite gender** | Avoid physical contact (handshakes, hugs) with Qatari nationals of the opposite gender unless initiated by them. | All visitors              |
| **Entering a Mosque**            | Dress modestly (covered shoulders/knees, women's headscarf) and remove shoes. | All visitors              |
| **Photography in Mosques**       | Always ask permission first before photographing people, especially those praying. | All visitors              |
| **Respect for Prayer Times**     | Be mindful during call to prayer; some businesses may close briefly.     | All visitors              |
| **Public displays of affection** | Avoid public displays of affection as they are considered culturally inappropriate. | All visitors              |

> **Qatar-specific:** Women should not initiate physical contact with Qatari men, and vice versa. Always show respect during prayer times by lowering your voice and refraining from loud activities near mosques.

#### 11d. Saving Face & Conflict Resolution

"Saving face" is a significant social concept in Qatari culture, emphasizing maintaining dignity and avoiding public embarrassment.

> Always approach disagreements with a calm and respectful demeanor. A public display of anger will be counterproductive and considered highly disrespectful.

> **Qatar-specific:** Raising your voice or showing visible frustration in public will be poorly received and can hinder any resolution. Politeness and patience are key, even in challenging situations.

#### 11e. Responsible Tourism & Child Welfare

Support local communities ethically and ensure child welfare.

> Do not give money or gifts to begging children or individuals. Instead, support established, legitimate charities or businesses that empower local communities sustainably.

> **Qatar-specific:** While begging is not common, if encountered, direct your generosity towards accredited local charities. Always ask permission before photographing people, particularly children.

#### 11f. General Social Customs & Greetings

Understand the common social norms for smooth interactions.

> Greetings are typically with a handshake for same-gender individuals. Modest dress is generally expected outside of beach resorts.

> **Qatar-specific:** The traditional greeting is "As-salamu alaykum" (Peace be upon you), to which the reply is "Wa alaykum as-salam". Public displays of affection are culturally inappropriate. Tipping is appreciated but not mandatory (10-15% in restaurants, small amounts for porters/drivers).

### 12. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION

Specific, actionable information for a safe and informed trip to Qatar.

#### 12a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health

Consult a travel medicine clinic 6-8 weeks before your trip.

| **Vaccine / Medication**           | **Priority Level**   | **Notes**                                                                                |
| :--------------------------------- | :------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hepatitis A**                    | Strongly recommended | Transmitted through contaminated food/water.                                             |
| **Hepatitis B**                    | Recommended          | For longer stays or those with potential exposure to blood/bodily fluids.                |
| **Typhoid**                        | Recommended          | High risk in areas with poor sanitation and street food consumption, though less so in Qatar. |
| **Tetanus / Diphtheria (Td/Tdap)** | Recommended          | Ensure booster is current (within 10 years).                                             |
| **Rabies pre-exposure**            | Low risk             | Only for extensive outdoor activity with potential animal contact.                       |
| **Meningococcal**                  | Recommended          | Especially for those performing Hajj/Umrah or visiting during those periods.             |

> **Qatar-specific:** Hepatitis A, Typhoid, Tetanus, and routine immunizations are generally recommended for all visitors. Malaria is not a risk in Qatar. Consult your doctor for personal recommendations.

#### 12b. Mosquito-Borne Illness & Insect Protection

Mosquito-borne diseases are not a major concern, but protection is still advisable.

| **Disease**      | **Mosquito Type**        | **Peak Risk**       | **Prevention**                                     |
| :--------------- | :----------------------- | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------- |
| **Dengue Fever** | Aedes (daytime biting)   | Hotter, humid months | Repellent, covered clothing, nets (less common risk) |
| **Zika Virus**   | Aedes                    | Hotter, humid months | Repellent, covered clothing                        |
| **Chikungunya**  | Aedes                    | Hotter, humid months | Repellent, covered clothing                        |

> **Qatar-specific:** While not a primary concern, occasional cases of Dengue or other mosquito-borne illnesses can occur during hot, humid periods, especially near standing water. Use repellent if spending time outdoors, particularly at dawn and dusk.

#### 12c. Water & Food Safety

Tap water is generally safe to drink in Qatar, but bottled water is preferred by many.

| **Source**                  | **Safety**               | **Guidance**                                                                   |
| :-------------------------- | :----------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Tap water**               | Safe (desalinated)       | Generally safe to drink, but bottled water is widely consumed and preferred.   |
| **Sealed bottled water**    | Safe                     | Readily available and recommended for peace of mind.                           |
| **Ice in restaurants**      | Safe                     | Typically made from filtered water in reputable establishments.                |
| **Filtered water stations** | Safe                     | Common in hotels and public facilities.                                        |
| **Boiled water**            | Safe                     | N/A (not typically needed)                                                     |

> **Qatar-specific:** While tap water meets international standards, many visitors and residents opt for bottled water for taste and convenience. Food safety standards are generally high, especially in established restaurants. Street food (e.g., in Souq Waqif) is generally safe if from busy, reputable stalls.

#### 12d. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness

Qatar is one of the safest countries globally with a very low crime rate. Visitors typically experience a very safe environment. However, it's always wise to be aware and follow local laws and customs.

**Overall safety rating**: Very Low risk for tourists.

**Most common issues**:
*   **Petty theft:** Extremely rare, but it's always wise to keep an eye on your belongings, especially in crowded areas like Souq Waqif or malls during peak hours.
*   **Traffic accidents:** While crime is low, traffic can be fast-paced, and accidents are a more significant risk than crime.
*   **Cultural misunderstandings:** Unintentional violations of local customs (e.g., dress code, public displays of affection) can lead to unwanted attention or legal issues.

**High-risk areas**: There are no specific "high-risk" areas for tourists in Qatar. However, being aware of your surroundings in crowded places is always sensible.

**Safe areas**: All major tourist areas, shopping malls, hotels, and residential districts are extremely safe.

**Transport safety**:
*   **Karwa Taxis (official)**: Very safe and reliable. Ensure the meter is running.
*   **Uber/Careem**: Safe and convenient, with driver tracking and cashless payment.
*   **Doha Metro**: Modern, clean, and extremely safe.
*   **Motorbike taxis**: Not common or recommended for tourists.
*   **Driving**: Qatar has a high standard of roads, but local driving can be aggressive at times. Defensive driving is advised if renting a car.

**Night safety**: Qatar is very safe at night. Walking alone in most areas is generally fine, but sticking to well-lit and populated areas is always recommended. Licensed taxis or ride-hailing apps are available 24/7.

**Scam awareness**: Scams targeting tourists are extremely rare in Qatar. The most common "scam" would be an overcharging taxi driver, which can be avoided by using the meter or ride-hailing apps. Be wary of unsolicited offers for "free" tours or goods, which are generally not common but good to be aware of globally.

**How to document each safety issue:**

ISSUE: **Cultural Misunderstandings**
WHERE IT HAPPENS: Public spaces, religious sites, interactions with locals
HOW IT HAPPENS: Inadvertent violation of dress codes, public displays of affection, disrespect during prayer times, using the left hand when greeting or passing objects.
HOW TO AVOID IT: Research and respect local customs, dress modestly, be mindful of public behavior, use your right hand.
WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: Apologize sincerely and correct your behavior. If a situation escalates, seek assistance from hotel staff or local authorities.

ISSUE: **Road Traffic**
WHERE IT HAPPENS: All roads, particularly multi-lane highways and roundabouts.
HOW IT HAPPENS: High speeds, aggressive driving, sudden lane changes.
HOW TO AVOID IT: If driving, be defensive, adhere to speed limits, and be aware of other drivers. If a pedestrian, use designated crossings and be cautious. Always wear seatbelts.
WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: In case of an accident, remain calm, ensure safety, and call 999 for police/ambulance. Exchange insurance details.

ISSUE: **Petty Theft** (extremely rare)
WHERE IT HAPPENS: Any crowded area like Souq Waqif, busy malls, or public transport during peak hours.
HOW IT HAPPENS: Opportunistic snatching of phones, wallets, or bags.
HOW TO AVOID IT: Keep valuables secure and out of sight. Don't leave bags unattended. Be aware of your surroundings in crowded places.
WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: Report immediately to the nearest police station (call 999) and inform your embassy and travel insurance provider.

### 13. SEASONAL CONSIDERATIONS

Qatar experiences extreme summer heat and pleasant winters.

> **Summer (May-September):** Temperatures regularly exceed 40°C (104°F) with high humidity. Outdoor activities are limited; focus on indoor attractions.
> **Winter (October-April):** Mild and pleasant temperatures (18-28°C / 64-82°F), ideal for outdoor exploration.
> **What to pack:** Lightweight, breathable clothing in summer; light layers in winter. Sun protection (hat, sunglasses, high SPF sunscreen) is essential year-round.

### 14. GENERAL TIPS

Practical advice for an enhanced travel experience.

> **Power sockets:** Type G (UK style) with 240V, 50Hz. An adapter is likely needed.
> **Wi-Fi:** Widely available and generally reliable in hotels, malls, and many public spaces.
> **Public transport:** Doha Metro is an efficient and affordable way to get around the city.
> **Working week:** The standard working week is Sunday to Thursday; Friday and Saturday are weekend days.
> **Ramadan:** During the holy month of Ramadan, eating, drinking, and smoking in public during fasting hours (sunrise to sunset) is prohibited. Restaurants may operate with limited hours or offer take-away only during these times.
